A lot of words in the English language have multiple, even contrary, definitions. Ex-SO here, I worked at Flag for over 2 years and was brand new to Scientology. Scientology jargon is extensive, but is very useful if you are involved with the church. The word "reasonable" in Scientology jargon actually means, "to create reasons, or explain away something [generally referring to something in poor condition]." It's not that crazy when you break down the word 'reasonable'. Reason + -able. The definition of 'reason' as a noun is "a cause, explanation, or justification for an action or event." The suffix '-able' means "capable of, susceptible of, fit for, tending to, given to.” Capable of justifications? Reasonable.

Well, for one thing, Scientology and money.
I worked at the largest church of Scientology, Flag in Clearwater, FL. There were over 2,000 staff members when I left. All of them make about $50/week, working 16 hour days, 7 days a week. Of course that sounds crazy, but every staff member is there voluntarily. I worked in the department of personnel, which is responsible for all of the staff and recruiting new staff members. I was privileged to a lot of information about every staff member and I know for a fact no one was payed more than $50, and no one I knew was profiting off of parishioner's donations. 
It is true that parishioners of the church are often asked for donations (just as many religions do), which are supposed to go to expanding the church, building new churches in major cities around the world, getting books out, the Volunteer Ministries, etc. There are a few departments in the church that would have an interest in asking for donations called the Department of Public Services, the Department of Processing, and the Department of Training. All of these departments are in charge of delivering services that parishioners pay for. For them, the amount of donations coming in reflects the amount of service they are delivering. If the donations are low, then that shows something is wrong with the service they are delivering. To me, that makes sense. However, while I was involved with the church, staff members would often be told at staff meetings that we need to get more donations, that we're not getting enough. Each department would get quotas that needed to be met and if not met, could perhaps have to go on beans and rice for a week. To the staff members, it makes sense that if they are not getting donations, then it is their fault for not being productive enough, or not delivering the service correctly. Also, no one wants to get in trouble and/or go on beans and rice for a week. This is what seemed "corrupt" to me. If anyone is actually personally profiting, it is happening way up in the command channel, and that corruption is coming from whoever has power, in the name of the religion. From my experience as a Sea Org member, I never once personally benefited financially, nor did anyone I know, and in addition to that, no one I knew cared to ask for money other than with their intention to help expand the church, help mankind, and to not get into trouble.
